newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY RADIO NOON HEADLINES - OCT 11.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY RADIO NOON HEADLINES - OCT 11.

text.p: These are the main headlines on Hungary's Kossuth Radio midday news. Reuters cannot vouch for their accuracy:

- The opposition party Fidesz proposed to the Prime Minister to suspend the privatisation process, saying the scandal over irregular payments to an advisor threatens the prestige of market economy and private property.
- The Parliament plans to introduce stricter rules for entry into its building.
- The opposition Smallholders' Party (FKGP) proposes an investigation in the central bank to unveil why the bank is posting losses.

- The Budapest City Council's interpretation for a recent statement of the Prime Minister is that the local municipalities would receive all the assets from the state to which they are entitled by law.

- Debrecen City Council claims 110 million forints from the state privatisation agency APV, saying it received less money than due to it from Vector Rt, an intermediator between APV and local municipalities in asset transfer deals.
